document: Supply chain / licence / reuse manifest (aceite C06-A07)
decision_reasoning: C06 produced no source file copied, forked, adapted or re-licensed from any third-party project. Every third-party capability the product uses is reached through a declared distribution installed by pip, never by copying code into the repository.

The independent OLS oracle used for validation (tests/fixtures/pro_workflow/ols_oracle.py, 377 lines) is deliberately NOT a vendored copy of statsmodels/scipy/scikit-learn. Verified: `grep -niE "copyright|licen|adapted from|based on|taken from|SPDX|derived" tests/fixtures/pro_workflow/ols_oracle.py` exits 1 - the file carries no third-party copyright header or attribution marker of any kind. Its complete import set, re-derived with `grep -nE '^\s*(import|from) ' tests/fixtures/pro_workflow/ols_oracle.py`, is: `from __future__ import annotations` (line 9), math (11), typing (12), numpy (14) and scipy.stats (15) at module level, plus exactly three function-local imports - pandas (246) and statsmodels.api (247) inside an optional library cross-check, and the standard-library re (348) inside parse_number. That list is exhaustive; an earlier revision omitted the re import. It is a first-party reimplementation, and its docstring states the constraint: 'Forbidden imports: modules.*, backend.*, frontend.*'. tests/pro_workflow/p04/test_oracle_independence.py enforces that mechanically by AST-parsing the oracle source and asserting no import name starts with modules./backend./frontend.. Vendoring a regression implementation would defeat the independence that makes the oracle evidentially useful.

Therefore vendored[] is empty and must stay empty until a future campaign deliberately copies third-party source, at which point that copy plus its licence text and upstream commit must be added here.

licence_determination_method.primary_environment: /home/tjsasakifln/.cache/modelapro-c15-dev/bin/python3 (Python 3.12.3) - a pre-existing virtualenv whose installed versions match constraints/linux-py3.txt exactly for every package listed below (numpy 2.5.3, setuptools 84.0.0, wheel 0.48.0 and the rest all agree with the lock). No package was installed, upgraded or removed to produce this manifest.
licence_determination_method.metadata_command: python3 -c "import importlib.metadata as m; md=m.metadata(NAME); print(m.version(NAME), md.get('License-Expression'), md.get('License'), md.get_all('Classifier'))"
licence_determination_method.licence_text_command: find <venv>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<dist>-<version>.dist-info -iname '*licen*'   (RECURSIVE, deliberately: under PEP 639 the licence file usually lives in a licenses/ subdirectory, not at the top level of the dist-info, so a plain `ls` of the dist-info misses it and must not be used)
licence_determination_method.rule_applied: A PEP 639 License-Expression field is taken as the SPDX id verbatim. Where only a Trove classifier such as 'License :: OSI Approved :: BSD License' exists, the classifier alone is NOT sufficient (it does not separate BSD-2-Clause from BSD-3-Clause), so the dist-info licence text was read and the SPDX id derived from the clause structure - the presence of the 'Neither the name of ... may be used to endorse or promote' clause identifies BSD-3-Clause. Where the text is a bespoke agreement, no SPDX id is asserted.
licence_determination_method.not_done: No licence below was taken from memory, from PyPI web pages, or from any SBOM tool. Nothing was installed.

dependencies.name: scipy
dependencies.licence_evidence: No License-Expression. Classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: BSD License' is ambiguous, so scipy-1.18.1.dist-info/LICENSE.txt was read: three numbered conditions, the third being 'Neither the name of the copyright holder nor the names of its contributors may be used to endorse'. Re-verified recursively (`find <venv>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/scipy-1.18.1.dist-info -iname '*licen*'`), not by a top-level ls: LICENSE.txt is the only licence file anywhere in that dist-info - there is no PEP 639 licenses/ subdirectory. The dist-info DOES ship sboms/auditwheel.cdx.json, a CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM naming three components (scipy 1.18.1, libquadmath 8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1, libgfortran 8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1); none of the three carries a 'licenses' field, so it identifies the native code vendored into the binaries but does not state its licences. Those licences were therefore NOT determined here.

Those native libraries are outside this manifest and are not redistributed by this project - they are dynamically linked system libraries. For reference only, the Debian copyright files on the inspected machine (`grep -ohE '^License: .*' /usr/share/doc/<pkg>/copyright | sort -u`) report a MIXTURE per package, not a single id: libpango-1.0-0 lists LGPL-2+, LGPL-2.1+, Apache-2, OFL-1.1, Bitstream-Vera, ICU, TCL, Unicode and a Chromium-BSD-style entry; libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 lists LGPL-2+, LGPL-2.1+, GPL-2+ and CC0-1.0. /usr/share/doc/libcairo2/copyright is a free-text Debian packaging note with no machine-readable License: field, so cairo is UNDETERMINED from this environment. These are the Debian packagings inspected here, not necessarily the versions an end user installs; a commercial release that bundles a native stack needs its own review of that stack.

candidates_considered.name: pyHanko
candidates_considered.dependency_kind: not declared in pyproject.toml; not in constraints/linux-py3.txt; not installed in either inspected interpreter (importlib.metadata raises PackageNotFoundError)
candidates_considered.reasoning: pyHanko does PDF digital signing (ICP-Brasil / PAdES style). The product does not digitally sign its reports today: integrity is asserted through the evidence bundle's SHA-256 manifest (modules/evidence_bundle.py), not through a PDF signature. Adopting pyHanko would be a product decision for a later campaign; C06 neither depends on it nor vendors anything from it. Nothing in this manifest should be read as a claim that reports carry a legally recognised digital signature.

notes: Scope and counts (stated explicitly so the two numbers in this file are never conflated). This manifest covers the 29 DIRECT dependencies declared in pyproject.toml: 18 in [project.dependencies] (runtime), 1 in the [project.optional-dependencies].redis extra, and 10 in the .dev extra. constraints/linux-py3.txt is a separate artefact and contains 93 pins (`grep -cE '==' constraints/linux-py3.txt` -> 93). Of those 93, 26 pin a direct dependency (the 18 runtime plus 8 of the 10 dev) and the remaining 67 are transitive distributions (altair, pyarrow, protobuf, pillow, pydantic, starlette, brotli, zopfli, tinycss2, ...). 26 of 29 direct dependencies are pinned; redis, pypdf and playwright are absent from the lock. Derivation command: `python3 - <<'EOF'` reading constraints/linux-py3.txt and the pyproject lists, normalising names per PEP 503 (`re.sub(r'[-_.]+','-',name).lower()`), printing total pins: 93 / direct declared: 29 / direct pinned: 26 / absent: ['redis','pypdf','playwright'] / transitive: 67. Those 67 transitive pins were NOT individually licence-reviewed for this deliverable; a full transitive licence review needs an SBOM tool that is not installed (see BLOCKED in security_supply_chain.md). An earlier revision of this file said '~80 transitive' with no cited command; that figure was wrong.

AMBIENT-READ LICENCES (document-level disclosure of what is already stated per entry). Three of the 29 direct dependencies - redis 8.1.0, pypdf 6.16.1 and playwright 1.62.0 - are absent from constraints/linux-py3.txt, so they are not installed in the locked venv /home/tjsasakifln/.cache/modelapro-c15-dev. Their licences were therefore read from the AMBIENT system interpreter /usr/bin/python3, at the versions that interpreter happens to carry. Those three licence determinations are consequently NOT tied to a shipped, locked version: the version CI or a user actually resolves may differ, and its licence is not asserted here. The other 26 direct dependencies were all read from the locked venv at exactly the version constraints/linux-py3.txt pins.

EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY CORRECTION. An earlier revision of this file asserted, for wheel and for setuptools, that the dist-info carried no separate LICENSE file. Both files exist, under the PEP 639 licenses/ subdirectory, and are now cited. The cause was running a top-level `ls` on those two dist-infos instead of recursing, as was correctly done for jinja2, weasyprint, httpx, requests and python-dotenv. Every remaining entry in this file that asserts a file is absent was re-checked recursively with `find <venv>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<dist>.dist-info -iname '*licen*'` across all 26 locked direct dependencies; the only surviving absence claim is scipy's (no licenses/ subdirectory, LICENSE.txt only), and it is now sourced from that recursive find. Separately, streamlit-1.63.0.dist-info ships no licence file at all at any depth, which is why the streamlit entry rests on its PEP 639 License-Expression field and makes no claim about a licence file.

Vendoring decision verification: `git grep -n 'sklearn' -- backend/ modules/ frontend/ scripts/` returns one non-import hit; the oracle's attribution grep exits 1; no file in this repository carries a third-party copyright header introduced by C06. vendored[] is empty on evidence, not on assumption.

No vulnerability scan result is recorded anywhere in this manifest. Neither pip-audit nor safety is installed and nothing was installed to obtain one. Absence of CVE data here is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.

Every version marked 'pinned_version' was read from constraints/linux-py3.txt. Every 'inspected_version' was read from a real installed distribution, and the two are identical for all 18 direct runtime dependencies and for 8 of the 10 dev dependencies - i.e. for all 26 direct dependencies that the lock pins.
Nothing in this file constitutes a legal opinion or a licence-compliance certification. It is a factual record of what the metadata and licence files in the inspected environment say.
